recognize_zh: 中央一顆紅血球比周圍大一圈，胞質佈滿細小紅紫色點狀顆粒（Schüffner dots），內有厚實胞質環與一顆染色質點的環狀體，符合間日瘧（P. vivax）環狀體。
features: Single infected red cell clearly enlarged relative to neighbouring red cells, with slightly irregular oval outline
Fine, evenly distributed pink-purple stippling throughout the host cell (Schuffner dots)
Ring form with relatively thick cytoplasmic ring, central vacuole and a single prominent chromatin dot
Only one parasite per cell; no appliqué forms or multiple rings
Adjacent platelet lying beside the infected cell (not intraerythrocytic)
describe_en: Thin peripheral blood film (Giemsa stain, high power) shows a single infected red cell that is noticeably enlarged compared with surrounding erythrocytes and contains fine, diffuse eosinophilic stippling consistent with Schuffner dots. Within it is a ring-form trophozoite with a relatively thick cytoplasmic ring, central vacuole and one chromatin dot. Uninfected red cells are unremarkable, and a platelet lies adjacent to the infected cell. Findings are consistent with Plasmodium vivax ring-form trophozoite.

ddx.vs: Falciparum rings are small and delicate, often double-dotted, multiple or appliqué, within normal-sized red cells lacking Schuffner dots (Maurer clefts only in later stages).
Ovale also enlarges the cell with James dots, but the host cell is typically oval with fimbriated ends; separation may require species PCR.
Babesia forms small, pleomorphic rings without pigment or stippling, may form tetrads (Maltese cross), and does not enlarge the red cell.
A superimposed platelet shows granular purple texture without a cytoplasmic ring, chromatin dot or host cell stippling.
